title: A watching user can userMigrate and re-stake ahead of the operator's batch, capturing APY denied to users who wait
description: `userMigrate` is permissionless by design (the frozen-state escape hatch). A user who is watching can self-exit the frozen source staker and immediately stake into the Active target, jumping the operator's batch queue.
impact: Sophisticated users systematically out-earn passive users across every migration, out of the shared reward budget. Measured 1666 bps edge (Alice 43.151 vs Bob 36.986 phUSD) with a 5-day operator lag.
attackPath: 1. Operator initiates migration; userMigrate is permissionless by design (the frozen-state escape hatch).
2. A watching user self-exits the frozen source staker.
3. They immediately stake into the Active target, jumping the operator's batch queue.
4. They accrue from the shared budget for the whole operator lag; queued users accrue nothing.
likelihood: medium — profitable for any user with a watcher; cost is two transactions.
assumptions: targetAPY non-zero during the operator lag.
justification: Low, and deliberately NOT escalated to Medium despite the larger measured edge than CLASS-005. The distinguishing fact is AGENCY: here the mechanism is permissionless and symmetric — any user can protect themselves with two transactions, and userMigrate being permissionless is a deliberate, load-bearing safety property (the frozen-state escape hatch). In CLASS-005 the harmed user has no agency at all because the operator assigns the slice. The same remedy (targetAPY = 0 during the window) fixes both, but a shared remedy is not a shared root cause.
recommendation: Set targetAPY to 0 between finalizeAndReset and the final slice, so no economic weight attaches to who lands first — and do NOT remove userMigrate's permissionlessness, which is a load-bearing frozen-state escape hatch. Note that this remedy also happens to close M-04, but the two findings have independent fixes on any other remediation path (e.g. gating userMigrate closes THIS one and leaves M-04 fully open).

orchestratorRuling.verdict: RAISED Low → MEDIUM. The auditor's proposed MERGE with M-04 (a0967cce…) is REJECTED.
orchestratorRuling.whyRaised: The severity-auditor demonstrated the Low was understated. The victim and the loss are the SAME across both findings: Bob receives 36.986e18 in test_ECON_A (M-04, Medium) and 36.986e18 in test_ECON_H (this finding, filed Low) — identical victim, identical harm, identical shared budget. Only the beneficiary differs, and THIS finding's edge is LARGER (1666 bps vs 1000 bps). C4 severity is assessed on impact. The agency argument — 'any user can protect themselves with two transactions' — describes a mitigation available to a hypothetical ATTENTIVE user; it is not a bound on the harm to the ACTUAL victim. Every MEV finding in DeFi could be argued away as 'the victim could have been faster'.
orchestratorRuling.mergeProposalRecorded: The severity-auditor's preferred disposition was to MERGE this with M-04 into a single Medium — 'emissions run during a staggered migration window; time-in-pool is set by slice assignment or by self-advancing, not by entitlement' — with two actors and two measured magnitudes, on the grounds that two exploitation shapes of one defect should not straddle a severity boundary and that merging avoids inflating the Medium count.
orchestratorRuling.mergeRejectedBecause: The dedup doNotCollapseRegister (from D-24) forbids exactly this pairing: DIFFERENT ACTOR (user self-advance vs operator slice assignment), DIFFERENT MECHANISM, and — decisively — FIXING ONE DOES NOT FIX THE OTHER. Merging would let a fix for one read as closing both. A shared remedy (targetAPY = 0 during the window) is not a shared root cause. Two Mediums, each with its own remediation.
orchestratorRuling.requiredCrossReference: Related mechanism, INDEPENDENT FIX REQUIRED — see M-04 (fingerprint a0967cceac39…, InPlaceNFTStakerMigrator.migrateIn, operator-assigned slice ordering, 1000 bps). Gating userMigrate does NOT fix slice ordering, and fixing slice ordering does NOT fix self-advance.
